clusters.name: RAD - Emotionally Withdrawn Behavior (Criterion A)
items: Rarely or minimally seeks comfort when distressed (DSM p.295)
Rarely or minimally responds to comfort when distressed (DSM p.295)

clusters.name: RAD - Social and Emotional Disturbance (Criterion B)
items: Minimal social and emotional responsiveness to others (DSM p.295)
Limited positive affect (DSM p.295)
Episodes of unexplained irritability, sadness, or fearfulness (DSM p.296)

clusters.name: DSED - Disinhibited Social Behavior (Criterion A)
items: Reduced or absent reticence in approaching unfamiliar adults (DSM p.298)
Overly familiar verbal or physical behavior (DSM p.298)
Reduced or absent checking back with caregiver (DSM p.298)
Willingness to go off with an unfamiliar adult with minimal hesitation (DSM p.299)

clusters.name: Pathogenic Care / Social Neglect (Criterion C)
items: Social neglect or deprivation in emotional needs (DSM p.296, p.299)
Repeated changes of primary caregivers (DSM p.296, p.299)
Rearing in unusual settings with high child-to-caregiver ratio (DSM p.296, p.299)

criteria.thresholds: RAD: Crit A (2/2), Crit B (>=2/3), Crit C (>=1/3), onset <5y, dev age >=9m (DSM p.295-296); DSED: Crit A (>=2/4), Crit C (>=1/3), dev age >=9m (DSM p.298-299)
subtypes: Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder (Externalizing) (DSM p.290, p.298)

epidemiology.prevalence: RAD: <10% in severely neglected children (DSM p.297); DSED: ~20% in high-risk institutionalized/foster children, ~2% high-risk community (DSM p.299-300)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: RAD: 9 months to 5 years (DSM p.296-297); DSED: neglect before age 2 years (DSM p.300)
comorbidities: Cognitive and language delays (DSM p.297, p.300)
epidemiology.prognosis: RAD: significant recovery with enhanced caregiving (DSM p.297); DSED: tends to persist into adolescence/adulthood despite improved environment (DSM p.300)

etiology.neurobiology: HPA axis dysregulation, glucocorticoid neurotoxicity (hippocampal hypotrophy, amygdaloid hyperactivity), decreased CSF oxytocin, excessive NMDA/AMPA synaptic pruning, frontostriatal dysfunction (Dulcan p.524-525, StahlNeuro p.33, p.151, p.269, p.453, p.556-557)
etiology.environmental: Severe social neglect, emotional deprivation, institutionalization, frequent foster care switches (DSM p.296, p.299, Dulcan p.525)

first_line: Environmental stabilization and placement with a primary caregiver (DSM p.297, Dulcan p.530)
second_line: Sensory integration occupational therapy (OT) and behavioral support (Dulcan p.530, p.1051)
Pharmacotherapy for specific comorbid ADHD/aggression only (Dulcan p.530, StahlKids p.6, p.42)
key_side_effects: No FDA-approved drugs for core attachment deficits; comorbidity-specific side effects apply (Dulcan p.530)
treatment.monitoring: Dyadic attachment security, emotional regulation, growth/malnutrition status, comorbidity response (Dulcan p.50, p.530)

high_yield: RAD is an internalizing disorder marked by social withdrawal, whereas DSED is an externalizing disorder marked by disinhibited sociability (DSM p.290, p.295, p.298).
Both RAD and DSED strictly require a history of severe social neglect or pathogenic care as a prerequisite (DSM p.296, p.299).
Minimum developmental age of 9 months is required to diagnose either RAD or DSED (DSM p.296, p.299).
RAD symptoms remit significantly with enhanced normative caregiving, while DSED symptoms tend to persist into adolescence/adulthood (DSM p.297, p.300).
ASD is differentiated from RAD by restricted/repetitive behaviors (RRBs) and intentional communication deficits (DSM p.297-298).
ADHD is differentiated from DSED because impulsivity in DSED is socially specific rather than general motor/attentional impulsivity (DSM p.301).
First-line intervention is strictly environmental stabilization and dyadic therapy (CPP, ABC, COS); pharmacotherapy has no role in core attachment deficits (Dulcan p.530).
